prompt: Implement ImageBorderPadder.addBorder, which returns a new image with a solid border of the given thickness painted around a copy of the source.
explanation: Padding an image means allocating a bigger canvas and copying the original into it at an offset, so the destination coordinate is always the source coordinate plus the thickness. Filling the whole canvas with the border colour first is simpler than working out which pixels are border and which are not. Color.getRGB() packs the red, green and blue channels into the single int that setRGB expects.
hints: The new image is 2 * thickness wider and 2 * thickness taller than the source.
Flood the whole output with color.getRGB() before copying anything.
When copying, the source pixel (x, y) goes to output position (x + thickness, y + thickness).
